_README: Nutrition values for ingredients that Thai FCD has NO entry for.
Kept in a separate file from data/thaifcd_cache.json on purpose: that file is
'what INMU published', and mixing a second source into it would make its
provenance a lie. Anything here is explicitly not Thai FCD, and every recipe
that uses one of these says so in its nutrition_source.
See concern.md C12. Two of the 20 detectable YOLO classes are affected:
broccoli, which appears here, and onion, which does not need an entry because
it only ever appears in direct-lookup recipes where the whole dish is measured.
IMPORTANT -- the two databases do not define carbohydrate the same way.
USDA 'Carbohydrate, by difference' INCLUDES dietary fibre.
Summing them as-is would overstate carbs, which is enough to flip a keto tag.
So 'carb' below is stored on the Thai FCD basis: by-difference minus fibre.
Both raw numbers are kept alongside it so the subtraction is checkable.

EXT:usda-broccoli-raw.name_th: บรอกโคลี, ดิบ

carb_derivation.note: 6.64 - 2.6 = 4.04, converting the USDA figure onto Thai FCD's available-carbohydrate basis so the two sources can be summed in one recipe.

EXT:usda-broccoli-raw.citation: "Broccoli, raw." FoodData Central, 30 Oct. 2020, U.S.D.A., Agricultural Research Service, fdc.nal.usda.gov.

EXT:usda-chayote-raw.name_th: ฟักแม้ว (มะระหวาน), ผล, ดิบ

carb_derivation.note: 4.51 - 1.70 = 2.81. Thai FCD's only chayote record (STD:586) is young leaves/shoots with all four macros null (not analysed) -- confirmed by direct lookup and a broader re-search this session -- so this is the fruit itself, sourced externally, on the same available-carbohydrate basis as the rest of the file.

EXT:usda-chayote-raw.citation: "Chayote, fruit, raw." FoodData Central, 1 Apr. 2019, U.S.D.A., fdc.nal.usda.gov, FDC ID 170402.

EXT:usda-pasta-cooked.name_en: Pasta, cooked, unenriched, without added salt
EXT:usda-pasta-cooked.name_th: สปาเกตตี, ต้ม

carb_derivation.note: 30.86 - 1.80 = 29.06. Thai FCD has zero pasta/spaghetti entries of any kind (confirmed by repeated search under multiple Thai spellings).

EXT:usda-pasta-cooked.citation: "Pasta, cooked, unenriched, without added salt." FoodData Central, 1 Apr. 2019, U.S.D.A., fdc.nal.usda.gov, FDC ID 168928.

EXT:usda-hyacinth-bean-immature-raw.name_th: ถั่วแปบ, ฝักอ่อน, ดิบ

carb_derivation.note: 9.19 - 3.30 = 5.89. Thai FCD has zero hyacinth_bean entries. The official Indian Food Composition Tables (IFCT 2017, ICMR-NIN, checked directly via the ifct2017/ifct2017 GitHub mirror of the published tables) has only dried mature-seed 'Field bean' varieties (codes B007/B008/B009, ~275-285 kcal), the same wrong food form as USDA's own mature-seed record (FDC 175210, not used here). This 'immature seeds, raw' record is the fresh-pod match the dictionary entry (category: vegetable) actually represents.

EXT:usda-hyacinth-bean-immature-raw.citation: "Hyacinth-beans, immature seeds, raw." FoodData Central, 1 Apr. 2019, U.S.D.A., fdc.nal.usda.gov, FDC ID 169234.

EXT:usda-cocoa-powder-unsweetened.name_th: ผงโกโก้ ไม่หวาน

carb_derivation.note: 57.9 - 37.0 = 20.9. Thai FCD has no plain cocoa powder record (only a branded cocoa-cream cracker product). Unsweetened baking cocoa is unusually fiber-dense, so the correction matters more here than for most entries in this file.

EXT:usda-cocoa-powder-unsweetened.citation: "Cocoa, dry powder, unsweetened." FoodData Central, 1 Apr. 2019, U.S.D.A., fdc.nal.usda.gov, FDC ID 169593.

carb_derivation.note: 5.52 - 0.0 = 5.52 (no fiber in cream cheese, so no correction needed in practice -- kept for consistency with the rest of this file). Thai FCD has no plain cream cheese record (only a branded cream-cheese cracker product).

EXT:usda-cream-cheese.citation: "Cheese, cream." FoodData Central, 1 Apr. 2019, U.S.D.A., fdc.nal.usda.gov, FDC ID 173418.

EXT:usda-baking-powder.name_en: Leavening agents, baking powder, double-acting, sodium aluminum sulfate

carb_derivation.note: 27.7 - 0.2 = 27.5. Thai FCD has no baking powder record at all. Used only in gram amounts of 3-6g per recipe, so its real contribution to a recipe's total is a couple of kcal -- tracked honestly via this record rather than assumed zero.

EXT:usda-baking-powder.citation: "Leavening agents, baking powder, double-acting, sodium aluminum sulfate." FoodData Central, 1 Apr. 2019, U.S.D.A., fdc.nal.usda.gov, FDC ID 172803.
